nodes.norm_label: primes_k0_sieve table (v2 mor shallow clone of primes_k0)

nodes.label: Prime partition equation p = 2^m + q^n
nodes.rationale: Fixing one base to 2 avoids the combinatorial explosion of general two-term prime power partitions while remaining rich enough (non-planarity, covering obstructions) and tractable to billions of primes.

nodes.label: Hit set H(p) and representation count k(p)
nodes.norm_label: hit set h(p) and representation count k(p)

nodes.label: Covering-system characterization of obstructed primes
nodes.rationale: Obstruction (k=0) is a covering system in the sense of Erdos: propagation rule q|p-2^k and ord(2,q)|(m-k) => q|p-2^m poisons an AP of m-values; obstructed = these APs cover all valid m.

nodes.label: Subgroup exclusion proof (3^n not in <3> mod blocking prime)
nodes.rationale: 3 is not a primitive root mod certain primes, so <3> is a proper subgroup of (Z/lZ)*; the forced residue of p-2^m falls outside <3>, contradicting p-2^m = 3^n. Blocking primes {13,37,41,61,67,73,181,193}, max 193.
nodes.norm_label: subgroup exclusion proof (3^n not in <3> mod blocking prime)

nodes.label: k-distribution fit (negative binomial, overdispersed)
nodes.rationale: NegBin (Gamma-mixed Poisson) wins because it is a Poisson whose rate varies across primes = covering-class heterogeneity; mean 1.882, var 2.249, dispersion 1.19 (overdispersed).

nodes.label: r-distribution (r = floor(log2 p) - k, misses per prime)
nodes.norm_label: r-distribution (r = floor(log2 p) - k, misses per prime)

nodes.label: Magnitude-stationarity of mean_k (~1.88, band-invariant)
nodes.rationale: The m available positions and the ~1/m per-position prime-power density cancel, so expected hit count is band-invariant; confirmed empirically flat across bands 2^30..2^39.

nodes.label: Index-difference / S-unit relation on Mersenne factors
nodes.rationale: For two representations 2^{m2}*M_d = q2^{n2}-q1^{n1}, d=m1-m2; primitive factors ell of M_d=2^d-1 (ord_ell(2)=d) give q2^{n2} = q1^{n1} mod ell, an S-unit relation keyed on d.
nodes.norm_label: index-difference / s-unit relation on mersenne factors

nodes.label: Index differences are parity-locked (all d even)
nodes.rationale: Within one prime every hit position m shares a common parity fixed by p mod 3 (ord_2(3)=2); enables storing the hit set as one int64 bitmask k-agnostically and dropping the d-vector.
nodes.norm_label: index differences are parity-locked (all d even)

nodes.label: l-adic power-residue symbol analysis
nodes.rationale: Whether p-2^m is an n-th power decomposes into v_l divisible by n plus unit part being an n-th power in Z_l*; informative filtration primes are exponent-dependent (l with gcd(n,l-1)>1).

nodes.label: m-tuple statistics per k (unshifted tuples, shifted shapes)
nodes.rationale: z_unif = residual vs uniform 1/N null; z_indep = residual vs position-independence null (expected = total * product of single-position frequencies), flagging co-occurrence beyond marginal commonness.
nodes.norm_label: m-tuple statistics per k (unshifted tuples, shifted shapes)

nodes.label: Additive decomposition of prime power remainders
nodes.rationale: Reformulate q^n = p-2^m as additive representation over F_2 / polynomial in prime indeterminates to bring in algebraic geometry and p-adic tools.
nodes.norm_label: additive decomposition of prime power remainders

nodes.label: Fixed-modulus / Hensel-lifting obstruction depth
nodes.rationale: Work in Z/ell^k Z: sumset {2^m + q^n mod ell^k} determines admissible p residues; obstruction depth = smallest k with no lift, combined across primes by CRT into structurally-obstructed classes.

nodes.label: Planarity question — can r=1 lattice contain a K_{3,3} minor
nodes.norm_label: planarity question — can r=1 lattice contain a k_{3,3} minor

nodes.label: Baker bounds on linear forms in logarithms (Matveev)
nodes.rationale: Mathematically valid but computationally useless here: B(3,5) ~ 2^{10^7}, leaving an unbridgeable gap between the ~2^37 search frontier and the provable bound.
nodes.norm_label: baker bounds on linear forms in logarithms (matveev)

nodes.label: Bit-weight filtration (bound r*log2 p, not r or m)
nodes.norm_label: bit-weight filtration (bound r*log2 p, not r or m)

nodes.label: Algebraic-geometry / etale-cohomology formalization (speculative)
nodes.rationale: Frames k=0 as empty fiber and the covering system as an obstruction sheaf / Brauer-Manin obstruction; Kummer sequence and Tate-module tower organize the power-residue computations. Explicitly aspirational, not proven to apply.

nodes.label: Modular covering filter (native hot-path optimization)
nodes.rationale: Precompute per-residue coverage bitmasks mask[q][p%q] over Z/12Z for {3,5,7,11,13,17}; a semantics-preserving shortcut that skips pp_is_prime_power_u64 only when divisibility already forces the result (multi-covered => not prime power; single-covered => base must be q).

nodes.label: Forward-seeded table / backward-search oracle
nodes.rationale: For n>=2 the parent q<=sqrt(p) collapses to ~13k primes; precompute q^n into a flat map so n>=2 and large-m become O(1) hits. n=1 is worst case (dynamic Miller-Rabin); mitigate with a sliding-window segmented sieve, sqrt(max_p) precomputed graph, and 2-adic binomial locks (p&7==1 for even n).

nodes.label: identity bucket partitioning (p_bucket_version, p_bucket)
nodes.rationale: Identity-partition source columns are omitted from the physical parquet schema and synthesized at read time from manifest partition values (per Iceberg spec); p_bucket_version lets a future re-bucketing land alongside v1 files without rewriting.

nodes.label: primeparts.primes_k0 derived base table + MOR sieve clone
nodes.norm_label: primeparts.primes_k0 derived base table + mor sieve clone

nodes.label: Native IRC catalog (LMDB-backed SqlCatalog)
nodes.rationale: IRC-forward: keep the standard REST surface (any IRC client can point at it) while implementation stays native; LMDB holds only catalog transactions, base tables stay Parquet + metadata.json on filesystem.

nodes.label: LmdbCatalogStore (CatalogStore over liblmdb)
nodes.rationale: LMDB single-writer/multi-reader MVCC fits RunInTransaction; UpdateTableMetadataLocation is a head-pointer CAS. Tradeoff: drops JdbcCatalog SQL-DB interop, kept acceptable for purely-local research; CatalogStore seam keeps SQLite available later.

nodes.label: pp-catalogd native IRC server (cpp-httplib)
nodes.rationale: Thin JSON<->Catalog adapter: reuses iceberg-cpp's exported internal serde for both directions so no hand-written serializers; metadata engine (apply updates, write metadata.json, CAS) lives in SqlCatalog not the HTTP layer.

nodes.label: Commit ordering — LMDB CAS last, single-writer
nodes.rationale: Parquet->manifests->metadata.json written to filesystem first, then the LMDB pointer CAS last = the publish. Under single-writer a CAS->0 signals a bug/lock bypass, not a race, so no retry loops. Two-table atomicity handled by committing partitions before primes.
nodes.norm_label: commit ordering — lmdb cas last, single-writer

nodes.label: CommitFiles seam (create-or-load + FastAppend)
nodes.rationale: DRY refactor of PublishTable fed by a single {schema, spec} provider so the writer's partition spec and CreateTable's cannot drift; retires the dead files.jsonl text bridge.

nodes.label: Raw-SQLite reader migration onto the catalog seam
nodes.rationale: source_scan.cc, preflight.cc, ui_iceberg.cc each read iceberg_tables via raw sqlite3_open; moving to LMDB strands them unless they resolve metadata through LoadTable, so consolidate into iceberg_util.h.
nodes.norm_label: raw-sqlite reader migration onto the catalog seam

nodes.label: mdiff_k{K} derived tables (p, hit_mask int64)
nodes.rationale: hit_mask (OR of 1<<m over hit positions, popcount==K) is the sole stored truth; d-vector, shape=hit_mask>>ctz, anchor coset, and prime_rank are all derived on read, never stored; table unpartitioned, physically ordered by p.

nodes.label: Doc authoring guidance (excise done work, no narration)
nodes.rationale: Excise things once done; leave high-level framing to the user; project is NOT primarily about k=0 or solely covering systems — those are tools that rotate in and out.
nodes.norm_label: doc authoring guidance (excise done work, no narration)

nodes.label: Native build & rootless provisioning (BUILD.md)
nodes.rationale: Provision the dependency stack from source into $HOME/.local via native/configure using the system gcc toolchain — no sudo/conda/system package manager for deps; GCC>=14 hard floor because iceberg-cpp v0.3.0 uses C++23 <format> and std::ranges::to.

nodes.norm_label: native binaries inventory (generate, sieve, catalogd, tui, pp)

nodes.label: Number-theory core (primecount/primesieve/FLINT/GMP/PARI)
nodes.rationale: primecount replaces Sage prime_pi; primesieve for generation (fastest L1-optimized 64-bit sieving); FLINT n_is_prime/n_is_perfect_power for the hot prime-power test; GMP backs mpz fallback and FLINT/PARI.

nodes.label: query Lua module proposal (design, not-yet-built extensions)
nodes.rationale: Field-name/record-oriented functions bound to a catalog-validated QueryService are the right seam: the same module powers preset run() bodies, an interactive REPL, and scripted batch queries without the TUI re-implementing query logic.

nodes.label: Schema-field-name value dispatch (the 'c' key, accept-sets)
nodes.rationale: Dispatch is purely schema-field-name based (no type/domain abstraction); each query declares a literal accept-set of field names, so a q_k cell can feed p-lookup because both are prime columns.

nodes.label: p-scan window as predicate pushdown on p
nodes.rationale: Value is exact (k==K); the [p_lo,p_hi] range is a pushdown And(Equal(k,K),GtEq(p,p_lo),LtEq(p,p_hi)) that bounds the scan — load-bearing because there is no max_k stat to prune on, so k=16 needs the window or scans to EOF.
nodes.norm_label: p-scan window as predicate pushdown on p

nodes.label: TUI data-query layer design (QueryService, two read paths)
nodes.norm_label: tui data-query layer design (queryservice, two read paths)

nodes.label: QueryService (LookupPrime/LookupPartitions/ScanByK/GroupCount)
nodes.rationale: C++ service + thin C ABI: TUI is C (notcurses), readers are C++; a clean QueryService object is also the natural Lua binding surface.

nodes.label: Two read paths (k-scan early-stop vs direct-parquet point lookup)
nodes.rationale: iceberg-cpp prunes at file/manifest level but does not skip row-groups within a file; k-scan early-stop dominates, but point lookup reads the selected parquet file directly with an arrow dataset filter to skip to the row group (~1.7s vs ~6s).
nodes.norm_label: two read paths (k-scan early-stop vs direct-parquet point lookup)
